## Proof

Let $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$, with Cartan subalgebra
$$\mathfrak{h} = \{\,\mathrm{diag}(a_1,\dots,a_{n+1}) : a_1+\cdots+a_{n+1}=0\,\}.$$
For $i\neq j$ let $e_{ij}$ denote the elementary matrix with $1$ in position $(i,j)$ and $0$ elsewhere. The standard functionals $\varepsilon_i \in \mathfrak{h}^*$, $\varepsilon_i(h) = a_i$, give the roots of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ as
$$\Phi = \{\,\varepsilon_i - \varepsilon_j : 1\le i\neq j\le n+1\,\},$$
with simple roots $\alpha_i = \varepsilon_i - \varepsilon_{i+1}$, $i=1,\dots,n$. The root space attached to $\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j$ is
$$\mathfrak{g}_{\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j} = \mathbb{C}\,e_{ij},$$
since for $h=\mathrm{diag}(a_1,\dots,a_{n+1})$,
$$[h,e_{ij}] = he_{ij}-e_{ij}h = a_i e_{ij} - a_j e_{ij} = (a_i-a_j)\,e_{ij} = (\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j)(h)\,e_{ij}.$$

The given element $\theta = \alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_n$ telescopes:
$$\theta = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_{i+1}) = \varepsilon_1 - \varepsilon_{n+1}.$$
This is the highest root of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$.

**Determining $\mathfrak{g}_\theta$.** By the root-space decomposition above,
$$\mathfrak{g}_\theta = \mathfrak{g}_{\varepsilon_1-\varepsilon_{n+1}} = \mathbb{C}\,e_{1,\,n+1}.$$
So $\mathfrak{g}_\theta$ is one-dimensional, spanned by the single elementary matrix $e_{1,n+1}$.

**Verification of the eigenvalue property.** Take $x_\theta = e_{1,n+1}$. For any $h=\mathrm{diag}(a_1,\dots,a_{n+1})\in\mathfrak{h}$,
$$[h,x_\theta] = [h,e_{1,n+1}] = (a_1 - a_{n+1})\,e_{1,n+1} = (\varepsilon_1-\varepsilon_{n+1})(h)\,e_{1,n+1} = \theta(h)\,x_\theta.$$
Hence $[h,x_\theta]=\theta(h)\,x_\theta$ for all $h\in\mathfrak{h}$, as required.

**Conclusion.** The root space of the highest root is
$$\boxed{\mathfrak{g}_\theta = \mathbb{C}\,e_{1,n+1}},$$
and a valid choice of root vector is
$$\boxed{x_\theta = e_{1,n+1} = e_{1,n+1}\in\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
